newsitem.title: USA: Next move on US-Cuba ties up to Castro - Albright.
newsitem.headline: Next move on US-Cuba ties up to Castro - Albright.

text.p: The United States is interested in thawing its relations with Cuba, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Sunday, but the next move is up to Cuban President Fidel Castro.

"There's nothing romantic about Fidel Castro," Albright told about 750 business and political leaders in Mobile, Alabama. "He is suppressing the rights of Cubans ... The way Castro treats his citizens is totally out of step with what happens in the rest of the world."
But Albright said "the United States would very much like to have a different policy toward Cuba," adding, "We are prepared, when we see definite actions coming out of Cuba, to examine our policies."

The U.S. government has a longstanding political dispute with Cuba's communist rulers. Washington and Havana do not have formal diplomatic relations and the United States has tightened a 35-year-old economic embargo against the Caribbean island.
In Mobile to give the commencement address for the University of South Alabama graduating class, Albright spoke of the need to promote global commerce by eliminating trade barriers.
She drew strong applause with her statement that, "If other countries want to sell in our backyard, they had better allow American businesses to do business in theirs."

Looking toward the European Union, Albright said the United States supported moves toward an integrated Europe and single currency there, but said it would be "harder to bring about than people expected."
